Molecular genotyping can provide useful information in the management of radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancers. For patients with BRAF-mutant PTC (thyroid cancer), treatment with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) has been shown to significantly prolong progression-free survival (PFS). However, due to the limited number of patients with BRAF mutations, further investigations are needed to understand the potential positive effect of BRAF mutations in radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancers while also considering their negative prognostic impact in radioactive iodine-sensitive PTC patients.

In contrast, for patients without BRAF mutations, molecular genotyping may not provide additional useful information when used as a standalone test. A more comprehensive approach would involve combining molecular testing with clinical features and other diagnostic tools to inform treatment decisions.

It's essential to note that the current understanding of radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancers is evolving, and further research is needed to fully elucidate the role of molecular genotyping in this context.

In summary, while molecular genotyping can provide useful information for patients with BRAF-mutant PTC, its value is limited when used as a standalone test. A more nuanced approach that incorporates clinical features and other diagnostic tools may be necessary for optimal management of radioiodine-refractory thyroid cancers.
